subject: humanities
passage: Among the earliest sculptures to show the Buddha in human form are works from Gandhara, a region in what is now northwestern Pakistan and eastern Afghanistan. Their figures wear heavy, deeply folded robes and have wavy hair and calm, idealized faces strikingly like those of Greek statues. Art historian Farhan Siddiqi traces these features to the Greek kingdoms that ruled the region in the centuries after Alexander the Great's campaigns, arguing that Gandharan sculptors inherited a Hellenistic tradition planted there by those rulers.
passage_b: That Gandharan sculpture draws on Greco-Roman models is beyond question; what remains open is the route. The Greek kingdoms of the region had disappeared by around the start of the Common Era, whereas most Gandharan Buddhas were carved during the following centuries, when the region traded extensively with the Roman Empire. The closest parallels to Gandharan drapery and portrait heads, moreover, are found not in earlier Hellenistic work but in the art of Roman provinces from that later period.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the argument made by Siddiqi in Text 1?

choices.A: By claiming that the Greek kingdoms themselves commissioned the earliest Gandharan Buddhas
choices.B: By questioning whether Gandharan sculpture resembles Greco-Roman art in any meaningful way
choices.C: By accepting the sculptures' classical character while proposing another source for it
choices.D: By suggesting that artists from Rome traveled to Gandhara to carve the sculptures themselves

explanation.why: Text 2 says it is "beyond question" that Gandharan sculpture draws on Greco-Roman models, so it accepts the resemblance Siddiqi describes. Its disagreement is over "the route": the Greek kingdoms were gone before most of the sculptures were carved, and the best parallels lie in later Roman provincial art. Text 2 keeps the classical influence but traces it to Roman-era contact instead of the Greek kingdoms.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This is closer to Text 1's view; Text 2 notes that the Greek kingdoms had disappeared before most Gandharan Buddhas were made.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 calls the debt to Greco-Roman models "beyond question."
explanation.C: Correct. Text 2 agrees the sculptures look classical but argues that the influence came through later trade with the Roman world, not from the earlier Greek rulers.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 points to trade and artistic parallels, not to Roman artists working in Gandhara.
